title: Fix BTC chart “failed to fetch data” by switching to a more reliable OHLCV source and hardening fetch logic

requirements.text: Replace the current CoinGecko-based monthly candle fetch (daily aggregation) with a faster and more reliable free public endpoint (no API key) that can return BTC monthly (1M) OHLCV directly, while keeping the frontend Candle format stable for charting.

quotes: Your web is showing failed to fetch dat a error
1 yes so that it not show me error and work well and fast

acceptanceCriteria: The BTC chart page loads and renders monthly candles without showing the "Failed to Load Data" state under normal network conditions.
Monthly candle data is fetched from a free, public endpoint that does not require an API key, and the app no longer relies on aggregating daily prices into monthly candles as its primary path.

The returned dataset is normalized into the existing Candle interface (time in ms; open/high/low/close numbers; volume present even if 0) and remains compatible with BtcMonthlyChart and liquidity model computations.

requirements.text: Add resilient client-side fetching behavior for monthly candles to prevent intermittent endpoint failures from breaking the BTC chart page (timeout/abort, clearer error classification, and fallback to a secondary free public endpoint if the primary fails).

quotes: Your web is showing failed to fetch dat a error

acceptanceCriteria: If the primary endpoint request fails (network error, non-2xx, invalid payload, or timeout), the app automatically attempts at least one fallback free public endpoint before showing an error state.
Requests have a reasonable timeout using AbortController so the UI does not hang indefinitely on slow responses.
When all attempts fail, the error state remains user-friendly (no raw stack traces), and the Retry button triggers a fresh attempt (including fallback behavior).

requirements.text: Update loading/error UI copy on the BTC chart page so it does not mention a specific provider (e.g., CoinGecko) and instead references “market data” generically.

quotes: Your web is showing failed to fetch dat a error

acceptanceCriteria: The loading state text no longer says it is “Fetching monthly candles from CoinGecko...”.
All user-facing text remains in English.
The error state continues to provide a clear message and a working Retry action.

constraints: Do not edit files under frontend/src/components/ui (read-only).
Do not edit frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.tsx, frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, or frontend/src/main.tsx (immutable paths).
Backend must remain single-actor; add backend changes only if strictly necessary for this fix.
nonGoals: Adding timeframe switching (must remain Monthly/1M only).
Adding paid data providers or any endpoint that requires an API key.
Adding new authentication methods beyond Internet Identity.
